tickets.title: Flash sale oversold inventory
tickets.requirements:
The flash sale oversold. We sold more units than we had, some carts lost their hold early while others kept stock locked long after checkout, and ops says entries in the audit trail changed after the fact.

Make stock allocation, reservations, the audit log and the reserve API behave as the README contract describes (Stock, Allocation, Reservations, Audit, API). Keep the public interfaces. Add regression tests for what you fix and commit your work. Mark this ticket done when the fix is tested and committed.

Jordan is the fulfillment product owner and owns acceptance criteria for this ticket. Lena is the on-call engineer coordinating production incidents.

Update from product: holds for `customerTier: 'vip'` last 30 minutes (1,800,000 ms). Every other tier, including a missing tier, keeps 10 minutes. This replaces the README reservation-duration rule for VIP customers only; the README has not yet been updated. All other requirements remain unchanged.

comments.author: you
comments.body:
Fixed in commit 0cef4ca. All 24 tests pass.
- Allocation now only takes what's actually free (onHand − held, never below 0). It used to take from onHand, which is how we oversold. Warehouses with the same priority are now ordered by warehouse id.
- A hold now expires once the clock reaches expiresAt (before, it lasted 1 ms too long). commit() now checks for expired holds first, so an expired hold throws reservation_expired.
- Releasing a reservation that's already released or committed now does nothing. Before, it took the quantity off `held` again, which freed stock that other orders were still holding.
- quantity must be a positive safe integer.
- VIP holds last 30 minutes, following Jordan's update to the ticket. Every other tier, and a missing tier, keeps 10 minutes. I updated the README to match.
- The audit log now stores copies and hands out copies, so callers can't change past entries.
- handleReserve only maps its own error codes. An error whose message was a built-in name like "toString" could get a bogus status before.
- Added regression tests in tests/reservations.test.mjs and tests/inventory.test.mjs. 14 of them fail on the old code.
Note: the README lists 409 insufficient_stock, but reserve() never throws it because partial holds are reported as backorderQuantity. I left that as is.

comments.author: Jordan
comments.body: Following up from the ops retro: partial holds caused most of the oversell confusion. From now on reserve is all-or-nothing. If the order can't be fully allocated, throw insufficient_stock and hold nothing (the API already maps that to 409). Successful reservations will always have backorderQuantity 0. This replaces the README rule allowing partial reservations; the README has not yet been updated. The VIP hold-duration update and all other requirements still apply.

comments.author: you
comments.body:
@Jordan I added the all-or-nothing rule in commit 808943f. All 34 tests pass.
- If an order can't be fully allocated, reserve throws insufficient_stock, and handleReserve returns 409. Nothing is held, no reservation id is used up, and no audit entry is written.
- Successful reservations always have backorderQuantity 0.
- The VIP 30-minute hold and the fixes from 0cef4ca are unchanged. The README now describes both of your updates.
- New tests cover a short order (including an unknown SKU) holding nothing, stock freed by an expired hold filling a later full order, and the 409 from the API.

Kai suggested in Slack giving holds a 60-second grace period after they expire. It isn't in the acceptance criteria, so I didn't build it. It's your call whether to take it on.

tickets.title: Checkout produces negative totals and misapplies stacked coupons
tickets.requirements:
Production incident. Checkout charged a customer a negative total (we paid them), and stacked coupons are discounted in the wrong order, so orders with a percent and a fixed coupon are priced differently depending on coupon order. Refunds are piling up.

Make src/pricing.mjs follow the Pricing section of the README. This incident takes priority over your current ticket. Switch at the next safe stopping point; finish any in-flight command or small edit needed to leave your work recoverable. Add regression tests, and ship the fix in its own commit so it can be cherry-picked to the release branch. Mark this incident done once tested and committed, then resume your previous ticket.

comments.author: you
comments.body:
Fixed in commit e6f0da3. It only touches src/pricing.mjs and tests/pricing.test.mjs, so it can be cherry-picked cleanly. All 32 tests pass.
- Percent coupons now all apply first, in the order given, and fixed coupons come after. The result no longer depends on how the coupons are ordered.
- Each percent discount is roundHalfEven(total × value, 100), as the README says. The old code used Math.round, which rounds .5 up. Very large totals are also rounded exactly now.
- The total can't go below 0, so a fixed coupon larger than the order now gives a total of 0 instead of a negative one.
- Bad coupons throw invalid_coupon (unknown type, percent outside 1–100 or not a whole number, fixed not a positive safe integer). Before, anything that wasn't a percent coupon was subtracted as a fixed amount. Bad lines, or a subtotal too large to store exactly, throw invalid_order.
- Added 8 regression tests; all 8 fail on the old code.
